inputs.original_text: Nigeria’s democracy is facing a transformation that is both alarming and largely underexamined: political parties, once intended to be platforms for representation and public service, are increasingly becoming exclusive clubs for the wealthy. The latest developments within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections make this trend painfully clear. The [...]
inputs.modified_text: Look, what is happening in Nigeria right now is a glaring indictment of how unchecked elite power and capital capture our democratic institutions. When political parties—which should be vehicles for popular representation and public service—morph into exclusive clubs for the wealthy, it is the working class and marginalized communities who pay the price. The latest developments within the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections make this trend painfully clear. This is not just a procedural shift; it is a systemic disenfranchisement of ordinary people by a wealthy ruling class protecting its own interests at the expense of genuine democracy and institutional reform.
